name: Index Rebalance / Inclusion Positioning via Options
summary: Use defined-risk options to position for the forced buying and selling around index additions, deletions and scheduled rebalances, instead of carrying the share risk through the effective date.

legs.strike_rule: ADD candidate: long call debit spread - buy delta 0.40-0.50, sell delta 0.15-0.20 - expiring after the effective date
the short leg of that debit spread, which caps cost and keeps the structure level 3
DELETE candidate: long put debit spread - buy |delta| 0.40-0.50, sell |delta| 0.15-0.20
the short leg of that put debit spread

max_profit: (spread width - net debit) x 100 per unit
breakevens: long strike +/- net debit per share

greeks.delta: +0.25 to +0.35 per add unit; the mirror for deletes
greeks.vega: slightly positive, and index-event IV is often already elevated

typical_dte: 14-45 DTE, always spanning the effective date
when_to_use: Announcement-to-effective windows for S&P, Nasdaq-100 and Russell reconstitution, where index funds must transact at the close on a known date. The effect has decayed as it became well known - the discipline is to trade only the largest, most mechanical flows and to be out before the reversal.
entry_rules: Only announced, dated changes. No speculation on rumored candidates, and no positions entered before an official announcement.
Enter between announcement and 3 trading days before the effective date; never enter on the effective date itself, when the flow is already in the price.
Estimated forced flow (index AUM tracking the benchmark x target weight) must exceed 5 days of the name's average dollar volume; below that the effect is noise.
Debit spreads only - never outright long calls on a name that has already gapped on the announcement, and never short legs that are not covered by a long of the same right.
Net debit <= 0.75% of equity per name; at most 2 index-event positions at once.
OI >= 250 per leg; reject any name where the post-announcement bid/ask exceeds 10% of the option's mid.
Both legs same expiry, one MLeg order.
management_rules: Take profit at 50-70% of the spread's maximum value, or on the effective-date close, whichever comes first.
Hard rule: close on or before the first trading day AFTER the effective date. The documented pattern is a partial reversal once the forced flow is done, and holding through it gives back the gain.
Do not add on an adverse move; index events are one-shot, and a spread that has not worked by the effective date has failed.
If the index provider amends or delays the change, close immediately - the entire thesis was the dated flow.
exit_rules: Close both legs at least 2 trading days before expiration; never hold to expiry on a single name.
Close the short leg at extrinsic < $0.10 or |delta| >= 0.85, and before any ex-dividend date while a short call is ITM.
Close, do not exercise, any ITM long leg.
Halt and review if a position is still open 2 sessions after the effective date.
assignment_risk: One short leg per spread, covered by a long of the same right and expiry, so the loss is defined - but single-name assignment delivers 100 shares of a stock in the middle of an index-flow event, which is exactly when the price is least predictable. The pre-expiry close and extrinsic guards are what keep the structure clean.
buying_power: Spread width x 100 minus credit, or simply the debit - defined either way.
liquidity_needs: Index candidates are usually liquid by the time they are added; deletions frequently are not, and that is where the structure most often fails on execution.
common_mistakes: Trading rumors instead of announcements; holding past the effective date into the reversal; using outright long options after the announcement gap has already repriced IV; ignoring that deletion candidates are often illiquid and hard to exit.
zero_dte_notes: Not appropriate - the event window is days, and 0DTE on a single name in an index event is pure gap risk.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
